summary:
Orbital Cleanup is an interactive 2D space arcade game designed to raise awareness about the growing problem of space debris orbiting Earth. Abandoned satellites, discarded rocket stages, and fragments from collisions pose increasing risks to operational spacecraft and future space missions.

Our project approaches this challenge through an engaging educational gaming experience. Players control a cleanup spacecraft, collect floating orbital debris, avoid dangerous obstacles, and transport collected materials to a recycling station to earn points.

The game aims to introduce players to the challenges of space debris management, orbital sustainability, collision risks, and responsible satellite disposal. By combining interactive gameplay with educational content, Orbital Cleanup makes an important space sustainability issue more accessible and engaging.

Orbital Cleanup: Mission Zero

Orbital Cleanup: Mission Zero is an interactive 2D space mission design and simulation game developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Space Mission Design Game.

The project aims to raise awareness about the growing problem of orbital debris and the importance of responsible space operations through an engaging, educational gaming experience.

Players take on the role of a space mission designer, tasked with planning and executing missions to clean Earth's orbit. Before launching, players define mission objectives, select a spacecraft, choose equipment and launch vehicles, and manage important constraints such as mass, power, fuel, communications, budget and mission duration. Once the design is ready, they launch their spacecraft into orbit, collect abandoned satellites and rocket debris, avoid hazards, protect active satellites and transport recovered materials to a recycling station.

The game evaluates mission performance based on objectives, resource management, spacecraft design and operational decisions. Players receive a post-mission report explaining their successes and failures, allowing them to redesign their spacecraft and attempt the mission again.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes complex space mission planning concepts more accessible through interactive learning. It helps players understand:

  • The growing challenge of orbital debris and its potential risks.
  • The importance of spacecraft design and resource management.
  • Orbital mechanics, satellite operations and collision avoidance.
  • The trade-offs involved in designing and executing space missions.
  • The importance of sustainable practices for preserving Earth's orbital environment.

Our intended impact is to encourage interest in space science, engineering and sustainability while demonstrating why responsible management of Earth's orbital environment matters for future generations.

Technologies and Tools Used

The project was developed using:

  • JavaScript – Core game logic and simulation.
  • Phaser 3.80.1 – 2D game engine and physics.
  • HTML5 and CSS3 – User interface and visual design.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and project management.
  • Antigravity AI – Development assistance and implementation support.

The game is designed to run directly in a web browser without requiring specialised hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Our creative approach is to combine an arcade-style space cleanup game with a simplified spacecraft mission design simulator.

Instead of simply collecting space debris, players must think like mission designers. They need to balance spacecraft capabilities, available resources, mission objectives and operational risks before launching.

The experience combines real-world-inspired orbital scenarios, progressive difficulty, mission evaluation, spacecraft upgrades and repeated design iterations. This makes learning about space sustainability more interactive and engaging than a traditional informational presentation.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered:

  • Scientific relevance and realistic space mission concepts.
  • Accessibility for players without prior aerospace knowledge.
  • Balancing educational value with engaging gameplay.
  • Resource limitations such as mass, power, fuel and budget.
  • Collision risks and the consequences of orbital debris.
  • The importance of protecting operational satellites.
  • Performance, browser compatibility and ease of use.

Overall, Orbital Cleanup: Mission Zero aims to turn the challenge of orbital debris management into an engaging learning experience while encouraging players to think about the future of sustainable space exploration.
